clue.text: Measure period covered by recent broadcast

indicators.note: a thing covered by another sits within it, so the period goes inside the scrambled word
broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters of recent are strewn into a new order

parts.note: a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: A media story: some span of airtime taken up by a recent programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the letters of 'recent' into CENTRE, and 'covered by' means the time word sits wholly within that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a metric unit of length, a hundredth of a metre, so a measure.

clue.text: Players thrown out

definitions.meaning: the actors in a production taken together
past participle of the verb meaning to fling or discard

explanation.definitionFit: The company of actors in a play is its cast, and a thing flung away has been cast.

clue.text: Snapper we employed producing this?

indicators.note: words put to work are used in a new way, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A paper's staff note that their own photographer helps make the very publication you are reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' rearranges SNAPPERWE; the whole clue also describes the answer, a daily that hires press photographers, and 'this' is the publication you hold, as the puzzle appeared in one.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily publication engages photographers, so the snapper it employs helps produce it.

clue.text: It's used on radio, as I state

definitions.text: It's used on radio, as I
definitions.meaning: the code word for the letter I in the radio phonetic alphabet
a nation, here the large South Asian country

explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators spell the letter I with this code word, and it is also the name of a nation.

clue.text: 2, say?

definitions.meaning: the answer to 2 down is a daily publication
to put into words or articulate

explanation.walkthrough: The '2' sends you to 2 down; a British tabloid daily of that name is an instance, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Express is a British national paper, and to voice a thought is to state or put it across.

clue.text: Son, given a reminder to trail about, got free

indicators.note: to trail is to follow behind, so the son and prompt come after the word for about

parts.note: re means concerning or about
s is the genealogy abbreviation for son
an actor cued is prompted with a line

explanation.surface: A boy reminded of his duty goes off wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone saved from danger has been set at liberty, released from a predicament.

clue.text: Casually grand, that's you!

definitions.meaning: informal slang for a thousand, as in a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.definitionFit: Slang shortens thousand to this, and it is the archaic familiar form of the pronoun you.

clue.text: So, here's where we may see this hyphen: 'centrally-heated'

indicators.text: here's where we may see this
indicators.note: the setter points to a stretch of the clue text in which the answer can be seen written out

explanation.surface: A grammar note: the dash in 'centrally-heated' marks a compound adjective.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'hypHEN CEntrally'; 'heated' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean therefore or for this reason, introducing a conclusion.

clue.text: Left-wing new university reflected Welsh town below

indicators.note: a mirror image runs backwards, so the left-wing, new and university letters are read in reverse

parts.note: red means socialist or left-wing
Neath is a town in south Wales

explanation.surface: A socialist new college looks back on a town in Wales lying beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns REDNU into UNDER. NEATH is a town near Swansea in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying beneath another is below it; the two are synonyms of position.

clue.text: Darned watch includes week and day

indicators.note: a thing that includes another has it inside, so the week goes within the word for watch

parts.note: to watch is to see

explanation.surface: A sock repaired while someone keeps an eye on the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: To darn a hole is to mend it with needle and thread, so darned clothes have been stitched.

clue.text: Put off work, upset by papa coming in smashed

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns things over; here the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: papa comes in, entering the word for smashed

parts.note: stoned is slang for very drunk, as is smashed
Papa is the radio code word for the letter P

explanation.surface: Someone delays their job, annoyed because their drunk father has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the musical abbreviation for work backwards, and 'coming in' slots papa into the slang word for drunk; 'by' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something off is to delay it to a later time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Calm wide sea

definitions.meaning: the largest ocean on Earth, between Asia and the Americas

explanation.definitionFit: The word means peaceable, and it names the biggest ocean, so called by Magellan for its quiet waters.

clue.text: Parking delayed Parisian at the top of the hill?

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
late means behind time
French au means 'at the', as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A late driver from Paris looking for a parking space at a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableland is a raised area of flat ground, an example of a level summit, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Go over chapter by nonsensical writer

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat

explanation.surface: Revising a chapter by a writer of nonsense rhymes.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over a fence or bar without touching it is to clear it, as a high-jumper does.

clue.text: Page inserted in Paradise Lost — second goes missing

indicators.note: the page is put into the word paradise
lost means astray, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone inserting a page into a copy of Milton's epic, but a later one vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inserted in' adds P to PARADISE, S joins, and 'Lost' rearranges all ten letters; Paradise Lost is Milton's epic.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to go missing; the third-person verb matches the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Brings in drink, singular — the setter's first

indicators.note: first says the setter's piece leads, ahead of the drink and singular

parts.note: the setter is 'I', so the setter's (the setter is) gives I'm
port is a fortified wine
s is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Someone at a bar brings in one drink, the crossword's author getting the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Imports are goods a country brings in from abroad, so the verb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Shocks rebels

definitions.meaning: disgusts or appals, as a verb
rises up against authority, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Something that disgusts people repels them, and insurgents who rise up against rulers do the same verb.

clue.text: Military forces from Germany and Spain cross swords

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
to fence is to fight with swords as a sport

explanation.surface: European troops from two nations engaging in a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's armed services are collectively its defence, as in a ministry of that name.

clue.text: Worse row follows twisted article that's horrid!

indicators.note: the row comes after the other pieces
twisted means turned round, so the article is written backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
ugh is an exclamation of disgust
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A writer's crumpled piece is followed by a worse quarrel, and how dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns AN into NA. 'Worse' in the sense of more badly behaved, as a child might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who misbehaves more than another is worse behaved, comparative of mischievous.

clue.text: After travelling, a driver did it?

indicators.note: letters on the move shift about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A motorist's journey ends; did they get there?
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges A DRIVER. To have 'made it' or 'done it' is to succeed, so the definition is fair with its question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has arrived has made it, achieving success, which the idiom 'did it' also expresses.

clue.text: Undeterred by river, welcoming suggestions to go over

indicators.note: the river takes in, or welcomes, the other piece

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means turned back, so the word for suggestions is read upward

parts.note: tips are pieces of advice or suggestions

explanation.surface: Someone ignoring river advice about crossing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go over' turns TIPS into SPIT, which 'welcoming' puts in DEE, the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means in spite of, not put off by something, so a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bill's memoir?

definitions.meaning: an invoice or statement of charges
a personal record or story of events

explanation.definitionFit: An invoice from a shop is an account, and a written version of what happened is one too.

clue.text: Settle on Scottish isle, say, to go climbing

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upward, so the letters for say are written in reverse

parts.note: eg (for example) is what say means

explanation.surface: Someone moving to a Scottish island and taking up hillwalking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go climbing' turns EG into GE; 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a matter is to organise or fix it, as in agreeing a date.

clue.text: Something from river put in ring?

definitions.text: Something from river put in ring?

parts.words: Something from river put in ring?
parts.note: a gem from a river mussel can be set into a ring, and the misleading picture is a stone tossed in a boxing ring

explanation.walkthrough: Freshwater mussels yield gems, which a jeweller mounts on a band; 'ring' tempts you toward boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gems formed in molluscs, including river mussels, are set in jewellery such as rings.

clue.text: With central heating left off, fortunate to be prepared

indicators.note: left off means omitted, so the central heating letters are dropped

parts.note: charmed means blessed with luck
CH is the estate-agent abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: Lucky to be ready even with the heating switched off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being armed means being equipped or ready, as in forearmed with knowledge.

clue.text: Mark's secure attic she entered occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Mark is securing the attic that a woman has gone into.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking alternate letters of 'secure attic she' from the first gives the answer; 'Mark's' is 'Mark is', and 'entered' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape or score on a surface is a mark, as in a scratch on paintwork.

clue.text: Beat broth to liquefy

indicators.note: something liquefied loses its form, so these letters melt into a new order

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: whisk the soup until it runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse or throb is a rhythmic beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Kept watch on, as I had to be picked up

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, as with radio signals, means heard

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A lookout's report on what they once did.
explanation.walkthrough: I'D, the short form of 'I had', is said aloud to give the answer; 'as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch it closely, so the past tense means kept a watch on.

clue.text: Entering confession

definitions.meaning: gaining entry, a noun sense of going in
an acknowledgement of guilt or of a fact

explanation.definitionFit: Being let into a place is entry, and owning up to something is an avowal of it.

clue.text: Liable to drizzle in amongst bit of sunshine?

indicators.note: the word in goes amongst the letters of the sunbeam

parts.note: a ray is a beam of sunlight

explanation.surface: A forecast asking if a damp spell sits in the middle of a sunny one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather that tends to bring showers is the adjective for damp, drizzly days.

clue.text: One could be right — it's fifty-fifty

definitions.meaning: the right one of two flanks
a half of something split equally in two

explanation.definitionFit: There is a right flank and a left, and each of two equal halves is a half, as in a coin's face.

clue.text: Recalled to be given a new appendage?

definitions.text: Recalled to be given a new appendage?

parts.words: Recalled to be given a new appendage?
parts.note: the clue invites reading the word as having been fitted again with a limb or member

explanation.walkthrough: Split 're-' plus a verb from 'member', meaning a limb, and it says fitted with a new limb; normally it means brought back to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brought back to mind has been recalled; the playful reading is fitted with a limb anew.
